name: COMP101_W5_W6
authoring_policy: COMP101 W5–W6: PATH (comp101_path_w5_w6.json) is the concept/method spine for /path/next — the tutor advances along PATH after each beat. Skills are practice units off PATH and use requiresConcept (not usesConcept). dependsOn is strict readiness. recommendedBefore is soft sibling pacing ONLY when peers compete and PATH/dependsOn do not already decide order (dilemma cases) — not for every consecutive pair. confusedWith marks student mix-ups. Concept-before-application: a skill's required concepts appear on PATH before the skill is practiced.

relation_semantics.requiresConcept: A COMP101 skill requires this concept if a student cannot perform the skill as taught in this Python course without it. A skill may require several concepts; each edge is independently valid. Optional patterns and language-general caveats do not count. Generic operations (Access, Update, Insert) are valid when the skill is about that operation.
relation_semantics.usesConcept: The subject method/construct/builtin relies on or carries out the object concept in a load-bearing way. Not for Skills (use requiresConcept). Teaching footnotes are not usesConcept targets.
relation_semantics.taughtIn: First introduction in this module's lecture/week. Week 5 covers lists and tuples; Week 6 covers dicts and sets.
relation_semantics.revisitedIn: Reinforcement in a later week after taughtIn — not first introduction.
relation_semantics.throwsError: An operation, method, or language construct can raise this error under realistic COMP101 conditions. Prefer Method / BuiltInFunction / LanguageConstruct carriers.
relation_semantics.implementsConcept: Syntax-level coding of a concept by a LanguageConstruct. Do not attach Pattern nodes or trait concepts via implementsConcept.
relation_semantics.producesType: The DataType returned by the method/builtin as modelled (e.g. str.split → list).
relation_semantics.recommendedBefore: Authored soft teaching order among sibling peers when there is a dilemma (which to introduce first) and PATH/dependsOn do not already decide. Not a strict prerequisite (dependsOn), not a confusion link (confusedWith), and not needed between consecutive PATH beats the tutor already traverses in order.
relation_semantics.dependsOn: Strict prerequisite: subject after object; student cannot reasonably understand the subject without the object.
relation_semantics.methodOf: The subject Method belongs to the object DataType (e.g. list_append methodOf list).
relation_semantics.misconceptionAbout: Dynamic: the misconception distorts this static concept/type/method.
relation_semantics.blocksSkill: Dynamic: this misconception prevents acquiring the named skill.
relation_semantics.surfacesInLecture: Dynamic: the misconception typically surfaces in this lecture.
relation_semantics.manifestsAs: Dynamic: the misconception produces this observable symptom.
relation_semantics.remediatedBy: Dynamic: the recommended remediation for this misconception.
relation_semantics.confusedWith: Entities students often confuse and should explicitly distinguish (list/tuple/set/dict/str, discard vs remove). Not for logical opposites or free alternatives — that is OOP's contrastsWith. Endpoints may be Concept, Method, or DataType when students mix them up.

competency_questions.question: Are list / indexing concepts present in W5?
Are dict / set concepts present in W6?
Are there dependsOn edges among curriculum entities?
